## Quick Start

```bash
# 1. Install Bun (required runtime)
curl -fsSL https://bun.sh/install | bash

# 2. Clone and install dependencies
git clone https://github.com/coleam00/Archon && cd Archon
bun install

# 3. Configure minimum viable environment
cp .env.example .env
# Set CLAUDE_USE_GLOBAL_AUTH=true (requires `claude /login` first)

# 4. Start server + Web UI (hot reload)
bun run dev        # server: port 3090 | web UI: port 5173

# 5. Verify
curl http://localhost:3090/health   # → {"status":"ok"}
```

## Key Concepts

**DAG Workflow** — A YAML file in `.archon/workflows/` that defines nodes with explicit `depends_on` edges. Independent nodes in the same topological layer run concurrently via `Promise.allSettled`. Node types: `prompt`, `command`, `bash`, `loop`. See [Architecture → DagNode](architecture.md#8-dagnode-discriminated-union----packagesworkflowssrcschemasdagnodets).

**Git Worktree Isolation** — Every workflow run gets its own git worktree under `~/.archon/workspaces/{owner}/{repo}/worktrees/`. The main checkout is never touched. Managed by `@archon/isolation` via `WorktreeProvider` and tracked in the `isolation_environments` DB table. See [Architecture → IIsolationProvider](architecture.md#6-iisolationprovider--iisolationstore----packagesisolationsrctypests-packagesisolationsrcstorets).

**WorkflowDeps injection** — `@archon/workflows` has zero dependency on `@archon/core`. The engine receives DB access, AI clients, and config through the `WorkflowDeps` interface injected at call time, preventing circular imports. See [Architecture → WorkflowDeps](architecture.md#5-workflowdeps----packagesworkflowssrcdepsts273).

**Router AI** — When a user sends a free-text message, a Claude call (with `tools: []` to block tool use) reads all registered codebases and discovered workflows, then emits `/invoke-workflow <name> --project <p> --prompt "..."`. This eliminates the need to remember workflow names. See [Architecture → Data Flow](architecture.md#data-flow).

**IPlatformAdapter** — The single interface all platform adapters implement (`sendMessage`, `sendStructuredEvent`, `getStreamingMode`, `start`, `stop`, etc.). The orchestrator never talks to a platform directly. Current adapters: Web (SSE), Slack, Telegram, Discord, GitHub, GitLab, Gitea, CLI. See [Architecture → IPlatformAdapter](architecture.md#1-iplatformadapter----packagescoresrctypesindexts117).

**SSE Event Stream** — Real-time progress is delivered to the Web UI via Server-Sent Events at `GET /api/stream/:conversationId`. Events include `workflow_started`, `node_completed`, `tool_called`, `approval_requested`, and more. The stream is ephemeral — subscribe before triggering work. See [API Reference → Streaming](api-reference.md#streaming-sse).

**Env-Leak Gate** — Before any Claude subprocess runs, `.env` files are scanned for API keys. Execution is blocked unless the codebase has `allow_env_keys: true` (set via `PATCH /api/codebases/:id`). Every grant is audit-logged. See [Architecture → Env leak gate](architecture.md#9-env-leak-gate-with-audit-log).

## Cross-Cutting Notes

**`@archon/web` type generation is a manual step.** After changing server routes, the frontend type file (`packages/web/src/lib/api.generated.d.ts`) must be regenerated with `bun --filter @archon/web generate:types` while the server is running. Forgetting this causes TypeScript errors in the web package that are not immediately obvious.

**`bun test` from the repo root is broken by design.** Bun's `mock.module()` is process-global and irreversible, so running all packages in one process causes ~135 failures. Always use `bun run test`. This is documented in CLAUDE.md and `dx-quirks.md` but is a frequent footgun for newcomers.

**`output_format`, `allowed_tools`, `hooks`, `mcp`, `skills` are Claude-only node features.** Codex nodes silently ignore them (log a warning). If a workflow targets Codex and uses any of these, expect silent no-ops — the integration guide flags this but the YAML schema does not enforce it.

**The SSE event stream does not replay on reconnect.** The event emitter is in-process only. If the server restarts mid-run, a client reconnecting to the SSE stream will miss all prior events. For resilient dashboards, combine SSE with polling `GET /api/workflows/runs/:runId`.

**Interactive approval gates require `interactive: true` at the workflow level.** Without it, interactive loops pause in the background but the Web UI does not know to show the approval prompt. The CLI always handles approval gates correctly regardless.

**SQLite serializes writes.** Under high parallelism (10+ simultaneous workflow runs), switch to PostgreSQL via `DATABASE_URL`. The `IDatabase` abstraction makes this a drop-in config change, but the `SqlDialect` helper in `packages/core/src/db/adapters/types.ts` is the only place dialect-specific SQL lives — review it when adding new queries.

**Worktree port allocation is deterministic but not conflict-proof.** The hash of the worktree path maps to port 3190–4089. Hash collisions between two different worktrees on the same machine are possible (unlikely but not impossible). Override with `PORT=<n>` if needed.

**GitHub webhook processing is comment-only by design.** Only `issue_comment.created` events mentioning the bot trigger workflow dispatch. Issue/PR descriptions are intentionally ignored (per anthropics/claude-code#96) — this is documented but surprises integrators expecting description-based triggers.
